expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jacoby Brissett struggled against the Giants last week, but we'll forgive one bad game. Dating back to last season, he's topped 20 fantasy points in 10 of his last 16 games and has two elite weapons in Michael Wilson and Trey McBride. The Lions are dead last in EPA allowed per play and success rate allowed. Both teams play fast and sit well above average in PROE, and the 54.5-point total is massive.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Brissett is a great GPP pivot to Goff who he faces off against. Cardinals are tied for 4th highest implied total on the slate and face a Lions secondary that has allowed the 4th highest EPA/pass (funny enough, right behind the Cardinals). Brissett has some really attractive pieces to stack with like Wilson & McBride.

players.notes: Massive 54.5 total. Faces a weak Lions secondary allowing high EPA per pass.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Arizona is weak in the secondary and should be able to score points, which should keep Goff fully engaged in this game for all four quarters. Gibbs will be a chalky play, so this may also be a way of getting slightly different.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jared Goff has always been tough to trust on full slates because the Lions have leaned on the run and played with big leads in the past. This season is the perfect recipe for his fantasy production -- the defense might be the worst in the NFL, and the team's pass rate over expectation (PROE) is much higher than in the past. Even with no rushing upside, Goff averages 21.5 fantasy points per game (FPPG) and 22.8 expected fantasy points per game (XFPPG). He draws a Cardinals defense that is dead last in EPA allowed per dropback.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Lions are implied for the highest total on the slate and Goff gets a matchup with the Cardinals that have allowed the 5th most DK pts and 3rd most FD pts to opposing QBs. The sims also have Goff as the highest Opto% which gives confidence for cash games minimum.

players.notes: Highest slate total. Faces a Cardinals defense dead last in dropback EPA.
Solid volume projection in a close 41.5 total matchup against New Orleans.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Sean Payton has taken over play-calling for the Broncos, and I think he's going to do two things they haven't been doing well. Throw the ball downfield and utilize Nix as a runner. He is a great pivot off of the chalk Jacoby Brissett on DK/Jared Goff on FD, and you can still get pieces of that game.

players.notes: Payton takes over play calling to boost downfield passing and designed runs.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I don't find the desire to spend down at QB nearly as great on FanDuel because the QBs are typically bunched close enough together in price that it doesn't make it worth my while. Maye has been dealt some extremely difficult defenses so far, so the Raiders won't be a shock to his system.

players.notes: Softer secondary matchup helps him settle in on the road as an underdog.
Strong passing volume expected in a favorable game script as heavy favorites.
Poised for solid pass volume as home favorites in a low-total matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Purdy leads the NFL in EPA/play this season, is likely having Christian Kirk sub in for Cowing/Watkins/Hodge and has George Kittle with full route participation. In a slate with very flat QB projections, I am in love with Purdy stacks on both DK/FD.

players.notes: Leads the NFL in EPA per play with George Kittle running full routes.
Tight divisional matchup with a solid 47.5 total to support passing volume.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jahmyr Gibbs has become the cheat code in DFS. He leads the league in touches (102) and touchdowns (7), and he's finally in the feature role we always wanted. He's on the field for 78% of the snaps, runs a route on 57% of dropbacks and gets all the key touches in the running game. The Cardinals have been tough against the run, but there's no chance I'm fading the best fantasy player in the NFL in a game with a 54.5-point total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs has an elite receiving role and touchdown equity to make him one of the safest cash plays week in and week out. He leads the NFL in redzone touches and 3rd among target share. He faces a Cardinals team that on paper has been great vs RBs but allowed 15 touches for 75-1 on the ground and 4-41 receiving to CMC.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs leads all running backs in expected fantasy points (XFP) per game by more than 4. This game has the highest total of the slate.

players.notes: Feature workhorse leading the league in touches and red-zone opportunities.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: With Kyle Monangai OUT, Swift is one of the better plays of the slate. He is available at a reduced price compared to what I expect his role to be as the Bears are one of the heaviest rush play per game teams in the NFL. I expect Roschon to mostly be a long down and distance player here vs GB.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: No Kyle Monangai so this should be Swift's backfield after he ceded work to Kyle in Week 4. The Packers have a bottom 8 run defense in the league, they lost Edgerrin Cooper to IR, and the Bears are one of the best running teams in the league. It's a particularly appealing matchup because the Bears are a zone run team, and the Packers have allowed north of 5 YPC against zone runs this season.

players.notes: Monangai absence leaves him as the clear lead back against weak run defense.
Projected for steady rushing volume in a close divisional contest.
Expected to handle early-down rushing work as home favorites.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Aaron Jones continues to dominate the backfield for this Vikings team, accounting for 24 of the 28 touches and 128 total yards vs the Dolphins last week. Since Mason Jones has been sidelined, Jones accounts for about 85% of the backfield work. The Saints continue to get torched by opposing RBs, allowing the most FPs and EPA/rush.

players.notes: Dominates backfield touches and faces a Saints run defense allowing most EPA.
Elite receiving and rushing upside in a competitive divisional matchup.
Poised for solid red-zone carries in a tight game against Washington.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: The matchup is pristine this week, and he has shown that he can be a touchdown-scoring machine when he gets looks. That style suits FanDuel better.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Michael Wilson has been an elite play, especially on FD, where his price hasn't gone up all that much however his production has.  He has seen 13 and 17 targets in the last two games and continues to get red zone looks.  Wilson is my favorite bring back option when playing Goff/Gibbs/ASB.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: The perfect pairing with Brissett in GPPs. Michael Wilson now has 30 targets over his last 2 games, yes you read that right. This Lions secondary has been burned by WRs, allowing the most DK pts and 2nd most FD pts to date.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Michael Wilson has established himself as the clear WR1 for the Cardinals, even though they used the 4th overall pick on Marvin Harrison Jr. in 2024 (and there are now rumors Harrison is on the trade market). Wilson has a 27% target share and a 45% air yards share, and his XFPPG says he should be having an even better season. The matchup is the best part: the Lions are signing dudes off the street to play in their secondary, and they've allowed more schedule-adjusted fantasy points to wide receivers than any team in the NFL.

players.notes: Clear WR1 with a massive 27% target share facing a struggling secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Cardinals have been torched by opposing WR1s; allowing stat lines like 5-82-1 to McConkey, 9-155-3 to JSN, and 6-112-1 to Nabers. After Goff failing to connect with ASB last week for a TD, I think this is the perfect bounce back spot.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I want as much exposure to the Lions/Cardinals game as possible, and Amon-Ra St. Brown is the easiest place to start. He runs a route on nearly every dropback, with a 27% target share and a 30% air yards share, and he does it with over half of his routes coming from the slot. He's been quiet in each of the last 2 games, but that won't last. He's one of the best spends on the slate.

players.notes: Elite route participation and a 27% target share in the slate's best game.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Under $5K on DraftKings is a great price tag, and his usage within the offense is ticking up.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: I was surprised to see that he is just $4900 on DK this week.  He's one of the best value plays on the slate and he continues to be a big part of this Bears offense.  I think he's a fine play on FD, but DK is where I am looking to be overweight on him.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Is Luther Burden the most disrespected 24% target share player on a good offense in fantasy football right now? He is better on DK than FD but still strong both sites.

players.notes: Highly targeted option seeing a Strong 24% target share in a good offense.
Strong projection for targets and route participation as an underdog.
Solid target volume expected as a heavy home favorite against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: The Detroit game is going to be popular this week and I expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be one of the more popular plays and with the price tags pretty similar for Amon-Ra St. Brown and JSN, I could see ASB being more popular to pair with Jared Goff.  I am looking to go right back to JSN who has shown he has an elite ceiling and he is someone I want exposure to every single slate.

players.notes: High-end projection and target volume in a competitive divisional total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Sean Payton has taken over play-calling for the Broncos, and I imagine we see a ton of usage going to Waddle. The Chargers have also had a lot of issues in coverage this year.

players.notes: Payton takeover expected to funnel a ton of targets into his role.
Explosive deep target threat with solid red-zone involvement.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Key wide receiver and running back injuries should give us plenty of value this week, so it's easy to afford an expensive tight end. Trey McBride is my favorite spend at the position, and he gets you into the best game environment on the slate. He has a 28% target share and a 27% air yards share, and his XFPPG is well above his FPPG. There's no better matchup, since the Lions are dead last in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to tight ends.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Lions have been torched by TEs, allowing the most FPs this season. TEs vs the Lions average 9.25 catches, 101.8 yards, and 1.5 TDs. They have allowed crazy TE ceiling stat lines such as 7-95-1 to Kincaid and 7-105-1 to Sadiq. McBride already sees a ton of volume, averaging so far 11.25 targets per game and gets a dream matchup. Play with confidence.

players.notes: Averages 11 targets per game facing a defense allowing the most tight end FPs.
Full route participation and Strong red-zone role in a 46.5 total game.
Elite rookie tight end drawing consistent targets in the passing game.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: If you can't find the cap space for an expensive tight end, Isaiah Likely is my favorite value play. His usage has been incredible in his short time with the Giants: a route on 81% of dropbacks, a 30% target share, and the first read on 34% of his routes. The Commanders have allowed the 3rd most schedule-adjusted fantasy points to tight ends.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Likely leads the team in route participation and target share both for the season and with Jameis at the helm. He also leads all NFL TEs in targets per route and percentage of team targets, and he's fresh off a game with 12 targets on 29 Jameis pass attempts. The Commanders are a pass-funnel defense that has blitzed at the 2nd-highest rate in the league, and they play almost entirely zone behind it. Likely's fantasy points per route take a jump against zone coverage, and in particular against two-high, which Washington predominantly runs. With their pressure, they're susceptible to big plays but also set up to bleed fantasy points to TEs. They have already been cooked by Dallas Goedert, Jake Ferguson, and even the Seattle TEs this season, and this sets up perfectly for Jameis to give us a ceiling game feeding Likely over the middle.

players.notes: Leads All tight ends in targets per route against a zone-heavy defense.
Reliable route rate and red-zone looks in a favorable road matchup.
Strong athletic profile translating into steady target volume.
Solid red-zone role and route rate in a high-total divisional game.
